==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*weh₁-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:verray>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|verray}}, from {{der|en|fro|verai|t=true}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|vērāgus}}, from {{der|en|la-cla|vērāx}}, derived from {{m|la|vērus}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*wēros}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weh₁ros}}. Distantly cognate with {{cog|ang|wǣr|id=true|t=true}}. Over time displaced the use of a number of Germanic words or prefixes to convey the sense 'very' such as {{m|en|fele}}, {{m|ang|full-}}, {{m|ang|mæġen}}, {{m|enm|sore|id=very}}, {{m|ang|sin-}}, {{m|ang|swīþe}}, (partially) {{m|enm|wel}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈvɛɹi/|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-very.ogg|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-ne-very.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈvɛəɹi/|a=US,Mary-merry}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-very.ogg|a=US,Mary-merry}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈveɹi/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈvɛɾe/|a=Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈvɛɾi/|a=Wales}} * {{homophones|en|vary}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛɹi|s=2}} ===Adverb=== {{en-adv|-}} # To a [[great]] [[extent]] or [[degree]]. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:very}} #: {{ux|en|That dress is '''very''' you.}} #: {{ux|en|Not '''very''' many (of them) had been damaged.}} #: {{ux|en|She's so '''very''' similar to her mother.}} #: {{ux|en|‘Is she busy?’ ― ‘Not '''very'''.’}} #: {{ux|en|In the end, the tickets didn't turn out so '''very''' expensive.}} #* {{RQ:Belloc Lowndes Lodger|II|0091 |passage=Then his sallow face brightened, for the hall had been carefully furnished, and was '''very''' clean.
There was a neat hat-and-umbrella stand, and the stranger's weary feet fell soft on a good, serviceable dark-red drugget, which matched in colour the flock-paper on the walls.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=13|passage=“{{...}} They talk of you as if you were Croesus—and I expect the beggars sponge on you unconscionably.” And Vickers launched forth into a tirade '''very''' different from his platform utterances. He spoke with extreme contempt of the dense stupidity exhibited on all occasions by the working classes.}} # Conforming to [[fact]], [[reality]] or [[rule]]; [[true]]. #: Looking back, I recollect she had very beautiful brown eyes.}} # With limiting effect: [[mere]]. #: {{syn|en|bare|simple|only|Thesaurus:mere}} #: {{ux|en|The '''very''' idea of climbing the ladder brings me out in a sweat.}} #: {{ux|en|[[the very idea|The '''very''' idea]]/thought!}} #* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=40|book=I|passage=We have many examples in our daies, yea in '''very''' children, of such as for feare of some slight incommoditie have yeelded unto death.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Paul Campos|title=The Obesity Myth: Why America's Obsession with Weight is Hazardous to Your Health|publisher=Penguin|isbn=9781101216590 |passage=Given the degree of fear and loathing inspired by the '''very''' thought of a fat body in America today, it is important to emphasize that all of the medical information in the counterfactual world I have just sketched is itself quite factual.}} ====Usage notes==== * Exclusively used [[attributively]] and never [[predicatively]]. ====Derived terms==== {{col|en |at the very least |at the very most |for very shame's sake |in very deed |the very idea |the very thing |under one's very eyes |under one's very nose |very same }} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|true, real, actual}} * Arabic: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * Georgian: * German: * Hungarian: * Italian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|the same; identical}} * Arabic: * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Latin: * Macedonian: * Nepali: * Norwegian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|са́мый}}, {{t+|ru|тот са́мый}} * Scots: * Scottish Gaelic: * Tagalog: * Zazaki: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|with limiting effect: mere}} * Finnish: * German: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Portuguese: {{trans-bottom}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=ervy|evry|ev'ry}} {{cln|en|intensifiers|degree adverbs}}
